title: ItemClasses
description: course/assessments/item-classes.yaml — teacher-defined pedagogical classes over assessment items (HW-D02). Each top-level key is a class name; each value describes the class's typical bundle. A class is a hint, not a lock: specific fields on an item override the class defaults.

typical_minutes.description: Typical range of item minutes for items of this class. Used as the reference for validators and the planner budget check. For low-variance classes (DIY, Practicing) the range is tight (e.g. 2-4, 10-20) and items in the class are expected to fall within it. For high-variance classes (Coding, Research) the range is wide (e.g. 30-90) and the per-item `est_minutes` is optional; the midpoint of the range is used for budget estimation when the item does not declare its own `est_minutes`.

default_tools.description: Tools an item of this class typically needs. Open strings — each must be declared in `course.yaml`'s `tools:` map (HW-D03). `class_tools_declared` warns when a class references an undeclared tool.

typical_bloom.description: Bloom levels this class operates at. `item_class_bundle_drift` warns when an item's declared `bloom` falls outside this range.

description.description: One-line human-readable description. Shown to the teacher during planning and on the student handout.

evaluation.description: How items of this class are evaluated in the /create-homework pipeline (by item-solver). Absent means fall back to item-solver's default: attempt if model_answer/rubric present, skip otherwise.

strategy.description: persona_attempt = item-solver attempts as personas and compares to model_answer (DIY, Practicing). execute = solver runs the item's tests via Bash (autograded Coding). skip = solver returns not_applicable and defers to teacher at Gate 2 (Research). custom = load a class-specific solver skill.

notes.description: One line explaining why this strategy fits the class.

custom_skill.description: When strategy is 'custom', the skill name to load (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md).

time_variance.description: Whether individual items of this class can be reliably time-estimated. `low` — items have predictable duration (DIY, Practicing). `high` — items vary widely per student (Coding, Research; a 60-min problem is 4 hours for a struggling student). When `high`, per-item `est_minutes` is optional and item-critic does not enforce tight timing; `typical_minutes` range is the reference. When `low`, per-item `est_minutes` is expected and item-critic sanity-checks against `typical_minutes`. Default: `low` if absent.
